stories.title: Legacy Partners Begins Leasing at Ontario Apartments
stories.excerpt: Legacy Partners has begun leasing at Mill House, a 346-unit apartment community in Ontario. Located at 2510 S. Euclid Ave., Mill House was built in partnership with DWS Group. Initial occupancy is anticipated in December 2026. “Mill House brings thoughtfully designed apartment homes and a wide range of amenities to the heart of the Inland Empire,” said Tim O’Brien, senior managing director for Southern California and the Southwest Region at Legacy Partners. “The community’s Ontario location offers convenient access to local shopping, dining, and major transportation connections.” He added, “Mill House is Legacy’s third active development project in partnership with DWS. We are also building projects in Scottsdale, AZ and Torrance, CA.” Designed by Architects Orange, Mill House consists of eight buildings with tucked-under garage parking and covered carports. The community includes approximately 6,000 square feet of ground-floor retail. Construction is anticipated to be fully completed in April 2027. The post Legacy Partners Begins Leasing at Ontario Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Legacy Partners begins leasing 346-unit Mill House in Ontario, CA; delivery Dec 2026.
Project includes 6,000 SF ground-floor retail; full completion April 2027.
Third active Legacy-DWS partnership; also building in Scottsdale and Torrance.
stories.summary: Legacy Partners and DWS Group have begun leasing Mill House, a 346-unit apartment community in Ontario, California at 2510 S. Euclid Ave. Initial occupancy is targeted for December 2026, with full construction completion in April 2027. The eight-building community includes approximately 6,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and represents the third active development collaboration between Legacy and DWS, with concurrent projects underway in Scottsdale, AZ and Torrance, CA.
stories.impact: Ontario's Inland Empire location offers strong logistics and transportation connectivity, signaling sustained multifamily developer confidence in the submarket. Retail integration and scale suggest developers view demand robust enough to support mixed-use density, particularly as e-commerce and last-mile distribution continue to anchor the region's employment base.

stories.title: Weil, Gotshal’s Collapse Is Perfectly Timed for Manhattan’s Office Market
stories.excerpt: White-shoe law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges, which was founded in 1931 and announced its intent to wind down operations this week, currently occupies around 447,000 square feet over 11 floors at BXP’s General Motors Building at 767 Fifth Avenue. BXP owns 60 percent of the 50-story building, which it purchased in 2008 in a joint venture with Goldman Sachs and Meraas Capital. Weil Gotshal has called the building home since it opened in 1968, and last renewed its lease in 2014. The firm — which employed around 2,000 people including approximately 1,200 lawyers worldwide — was a pioneer in the field of bankruptcy and restructuring, having worked with the likes of Enron, Drexel Burnham Lambert, General Motors and Lehman Brothers, and one of the country’s 30 largest law firms as of just last year, bringing in nearly $2.1 billion in revenue. With the surprise announcement of the firm’s dissolution after a series of partner defections and the failure of a proposed merger with Willkie Farr & Gallagher, the future of its 447,000 square feet of Class A office space — for which the firm is committed until 2034 — is suddenly up in the air, leaving a potentially sizable hole in the otherwise booming and largely occupied Class A Manhattan office market. (Bloomberg reported that Weil associates and staff were told they would be paid for 90 days, and that a more detailed plan for the wind-down would be voted on within days. Weil also announced that it will continue serving clients during the wind-down period.) Manhattan’s office market has enjoyed a strong year, with Savills placing the borough’s leasing activity through the end of the third quarter at 33.5 million square feet, up 5.6 percent from the same time last year despite rapidly shrinking supply for Class A and trophy space. The company noted that legal services was one of the industry sectors driving the strong demand. Prominent leases from law firms in 2026 have included Simpson Thacher & Bartlett taking 916,000
bullets: Weil, Gotshal & Manges winding down; vacating 447,000 SF at GM Building, Manhattan.
BXP-owned (60%) 50-story office tower loses 11-floor anchor tenant since 1968.
Firm was top-30 U.S. law firm; ~1,200 lawyers, $2.1B revenue last year.
stories.summary: White-shoe law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges announced its dissolution after partner defections and a failed merger, releasing approximately 447,000 square feet across 11 floors at Boston Properties' General Motors Building (767 Fifth Avenue) in Midtown Manhattan. The firm had occupied the space since the building opened in 1968 and last renewed its lease in 2014. Weil Gotshal employed roughly 2,000 people worldwide, including 1,200 lawyers, and generated nearly $2.1 billion in revenue as recently as last year.
stories.impact: 447,000 SF of prime Class A office space is flooding back to a distressed Manhattan market with elevated vacancy and downward rent pressure. The loss of an anchor tenant signals accelerating flight of large professional services firms, likely forcing BXP to offer aggressive concessions or pursue conversion—reducing institutional investor returns and capital availability for new multifamily development in Manhattan. Concurrent office-to-residential conversions elsewhere in the city may ease multifamily supply pressure but signal capital reallocation away from office-heavy neighborhoods.

stories.title: 200-Unit Affordable Housing Project Planned in North Seattle
stories.excerpt: Affordable housing developer Bellwether Housing and nonprofit Chief Seattle Club will partner on a 200-unit multifamily project in Seattle’s Licton Springs neighborhood. Delivery for the project, called Thunderbird Nest, is scheduled for 2029. The total estimated construction cost is $74.5 million, reported the Puget Sound Business Journal. The majority of the units would be two-, three- and four-bedroom apartments. The project is set to be built on vacant land purchased from North Seattle College. The Washington State Board for Community and Technical Colleges approved the sale of the site at 9250 College Way N. to Bellwether and Chief Seattle Club for $7.1 million in June 2024. Funding would be provided by the Seattle Office of Housing, King County Department of Community and Human Services and the Washington State Housing Trust Fund. Chief Seattle Club would provide on- and off-site services that are culturally responsive to Native American and Alaska Native communities. The post 200-Unit Affordable Housing Project Planned in North Seattle appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Bellwether Housing & Chief Seattle Club build 200-unit affordable project in Seattle; $74.5M cost.
Thunderbird Nest delivery 2029; majority 2-, 3-, 4-bedroom units; site acquired from North Seattle College.
Funded by Seattle Office of Housing, King County, WA State Housing Trust Fund.
stories.summary: Bellwether Housing and nonprofit Chief Seattle Club are partnering on Thunderbird Nest, a 200-unit affordable multifamily project in Seattle's Licton Springs neighborhood, with delivery scheduled for 2029. The total estimated construction cost is $74.5 million. The project will be built on vacant land purchased from North Seattle College for $7.1 million in June 2024, and will feature primarily two-, three-, and four-bedroom apartments with culturally responsive services targeting Native American and Alaska Native communities.
stories.impact: Strong public capital allocation and nonprofit partnerships indicate Seattle's policy commitment to affordable supply creation in the north end, reducing net new market-rate absorption pressure in this submarket. However, the 2029 timeline and public-sector funding structure suggest slower delivery than market-rate competitors, potentially offsetting supply gains and supporting rent growth in intervening years as demand continues to outpace private development.

stories.title: Simon to Acquire University Village Retail Center in Seattle
stories.excerpt: Simon announced that a Simon subsidiary has entered into an agreement to acquire University Village, an open-air retail center in Seattle, Washington. Since opening in the 1950s, University Village has been a Seattle community hub. Located north of downtown near the University of Washington, the open-air shopping and dining destination features more than 100 businesses and services. It offers a curated mix of signature national brands, local boutiques, restaurants, and other businesses, including Apple, RH Gallery, Crate & Barrel, Room & Board, Sézane, Lululemon, Aritzia, Vuori, and Din Tai Fung. “The Village began as an approximately 300,000-square-foot property, but it was never just about bricks and mortar; it was built around a vision of delivering an exceptional customer experience,” said Susie Plummer, Partner and General Manager, University Village. “Today, it has grown to nearly 600,000 square feet.” The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. The post Simon to Acquire University Village Retail Center in Seattle appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Simon Property Group acquires University Village retail, Seattle; ~600,000 SF open-air center.
Property features 100+ tenants (Apple, RH Gallery, Lululemon, Din Tai Fung); close Q4 2026.
Center located north of downtown near University of Washington campus.
stories.summary: Simon Property Group has entered into an agreement to acquire University Village, a 600,000-square-foot open-air retail center in Seattle located north of downtown near the University of Washington. The center features more than 100 businesses including national brands (Apple, RH Gallery, Crate & Barrel, Lululemon) and local boutiques, plus dining options like Din Tai Fung. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.
stories.impact: Simon's acquisition of a mature, irreplaceable UW-adjacent retail destination signals confidence in Seattle's consumer spending and foot traffic durability. For multifamily developers, stable retail/mixed-use infrastructure near universities reinforces demand fundamentals for student and young-professional housing in the U-District and surrounding neighborhoods, supporting rent resilience and capital deployment decisions in the near-term.

stories.title: Rexford Trades Newly Developed Fullerton Industrial to Owner-User
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield arranged the acquisition of a 136,218-square-foot industrial facility located at 1500 S Raymond Ave., less than a mile from the buyer’s headquarters. Terra Universal, Inc. purchased the property for $50,224,160 from Rexford Industrial, which sold the recently completed property vacant. The Cushman & Wakefield team of Kevin Turner and Jiselle Roberson represented the buyer. Representing Rexford were Cushman & Wakefield’s Randy Ellison, Brett Lockwood, Kyle McGillen, and Andrew Ryan. “By leveraging insights from the seller’s public investor communications, our team was able to identify a unique acquisition opportunity that directly supported our client’s operational and financial objectives,” said Turner. “The facility’s scale, quality, and location create significant long-term value for our client and gives them greater long-term control over their occupancy costs.” Previously, Terra Universal, an industrial machinery and cleanroom manufacturer, operated from two separate leased facilities exceeding 180,000 square feet, which presented operational inefficiencies and increased long-term occupancy costs. The post Rexford Trades Newly Developed Fullerton Industrial to Owner-User appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Terra Universal purchases 136,218 SF completed industrial facility, Fullerton, CA for $50.2M from Rexford.
Owner-user consolidates two leased facilities (180K+ SF) into single owned asset.
Sale highlights industrial demand and owner-user flight from leasing to purchase.
stories.summary: Terra Universal, an industrial machinery and cleanroom manufacturer, acquired a newly completed 136,218-square-foot industrial facility at 1500 S. Raymond Ave. in Fullerton, California from Rexford Industrial for $50.2 million. The purchase allows Terra Universal to consolidate operations from two separate leased facilities exceeding 180,000 square feet, reducing operational inefficiencies and long-term occupancy costs. Cushman & Wakefield brokered the transaction on both sides.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. However, the owner-user consolidation and flight from leasing signal confidence in Fullerton's industrial logistics hub and suggest strong local employment base; this indirectly supports residential demand in Orange County submarkets near employment centers, supporting demand fundamentals for multifamily development in Fullerton and adjacent areas.

stories.title: Attleboro Golf Course Poised for Sale as Redevelopment Opportunity
stories.excerpt: After more than seven decades as a fixture in the Attleboro, MA community, Stone-E-Lea Golf Course is preparing to close at the end of 2026. Attention now turns to the future of the approximately 140-acre, family-owned site at 1411 County St. and the opportunities it presents for redevelopment. To oversee the property’s sale and redevelopment marketing efforts, the ownership has tapped 128 CRE, a Massachusetts-based commercial real estate brokerage and advisory firm. SVP David P. Linehan, SIOR, will lead the assignment alongside Adam T. Meixner, Jeremy A. Freid, SIOR, and Tyler J. Capecci, SIOR. “Stone-E-Lea has been part of the Attleboro community for more than seven decades, and its history deserves to be recognized as we look toward the future of the property,” said Linehan. “Opportunities of this scale, particularly with visibility along Interstate 95, are extremely rare. We’re looking forward to working with the ownership and prospective developers to identify the best path forward for this unique property.” The post Attleboro Golf Course Poised for Sale as Redevelopment Opportunity appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Stone-E-Lea Golf Course, Attleboro MA closing end of 2026; 140-acre site on I-95.
128 CRE hired to market property for redevelopment; rare large-scale opportunity.
I-95 visibility and scale positioning for mixed-use or residential development.
stories.summary: After more than 70 years as a community fixture, Stone-E-Lea Golf Course in Attleboro, Massachusetts is preparing to close at the end of 2026. The approximately 140-acre site at 1411 County Street is being marketed by 128 CRE for redevelopment. The property's I-95 visibility and scale are noted as rare redevelopment opportunities in the market.
stories.impact: 140 acres of vacant land on I-95 in the Boston metro fringe represents a rare greenfield opportunity for multifamily development. Proximity to Interstate 95 provides strong commuter access to Rhode Island and northern Massachusetts employment; demand signals for suburban workforce housing in the region support feasibility of mid-to-large scale apartment development, particularly if zoning can be secured for density.

stories.title: Irvine Company Secures $157M Multifamily Refi in L.A.’s Playa Vista
stories.excerpt: Irvine Company has secured a $157.2 million refinancing loan from Capital One for a 309-unit luxury apartment property in Los Angeles’ Playa Vista neighborhood. The new Fannie Mae loan replaces a previous $136 million loan originated by PGIM, representing a roughly $21 million increase in financing, according to Yardi Matrix data cited by Multihousing News. The terms and maturity date of the new loan were not disclosed. The property, Villas at Playa Vista – Montecito, opened in 2016 at 12855 Runway Road. The community features one- and two-bedroom apartments averaging 1,113 square feet, along with a swimming pool, a fitness center, coworking space and conference rooms. Irvine Company acquired the land from Brookfield in 2015, and developed the building alongside two other apartment communities: the 703-unit Sausalito and the 491-unit Malibu. The three properties total 1,503 apartments. The communities are part of the larger, 460-acre Playa Vista master-planned development, which transformed land formerly occupied by Howard Hughes’ aerospace operations. The neighborhood now includes more than 6,000 apartments, approximately 3 million square feet of office space and more than 200,000 square feet of retail. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Irvine Company secures $157.2M Fannie Mae refi (Capital One) for 309-unit Playa Vista luxury property.
Loan increases from $136M PGIM loan; ~$21M additional financing; property opened 2016.
Villas at Playa Vista – Montecito; 1- and 2-BR averaging 1,113 SF.
stories.summary: Irvine Company has secured a $157.2 million Fannie Mae refinancing loan from Capital One for the 309-unit luxury apartment property Villas at Playa Vista – Montecito, located at 12855 Runway Road in Los Angeles. The new loan replaces a previous $136 million PGIM loan, representing approximately $21 million in additional financing. The property, which opened in 2016, features one- and two-bedroom apartments averaging 1,113 square feet, along with amenities including a pool, fitness center, and coworking space.
stories.impact: Successful refi of a 2016-vintage luxury property reflects strong debt appetite for stabilized Playa Vista apartments and signals continued institutional confidence in L.A.'s west-side rental market. Additional $21M leverage suggests property appreciation and rental growth; demonstrates Fannie Mae's continued engagement in Playa Vista and similar master-planned, mixed-use environments—supporting capital availability and underwriting feasibility for new multifamily development in the submarket.

stories.title: Grassroots Analytics Doubles D.C. Footprint With 25K-SF Office Lease
stories.excerpt: Grassroots Analytics has signed a 24,692-square-foot office lease spanning three floors at Arch Square in Downtown Washington, D.C. The company will more than double its footprint in the city as it relocates to 803 Seventh Street NW, a mixed-use property owned by Swiss real estate investment foundation AFIAA. The transaction brings the building’s office component to 100 percent occupied. The lease terms and asking rent were not disclosed. Avison Young‘s Greg Tomasso and Macy Parana represented AFIAA in the lease. Sean Balile, Jake Payne and Whitney Huang of Clarity Tenant Representation represented Grassroots Analytics. “Achieving full occupancy is a meaningful milestone, particularly in today’s office market,” Tomasso said in a statement. “The lease not only strengthens Arch Square’s tenant roster but also demonstrates that demand exists for the right product in the right location.” The deal comes as D.C.’s office leasing market shows improvement. Leasing volume increased 21 percent in the third quarter compared to the same period last year, according to Avison Young. Despite reaching full office occupancy, Arch Square still has approximately 25,000 square feet of specialized space available. AFIAA is marketing the space to retailers and prospective tenants that might be considering creative offices, showrooms or other uses. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Grassroots Analytics leases 24,692 SF (3 floors) at Arch Square, Downtown D.C.; lease terms undisclosed.
Tenant doubles DC footprint, relocating to 803 Seventh Street NW (AFIAA-owned property).
Building achieves 100% office occupancy; D.C. Q3 leasing volume up 21% YoY.
stories.summary: Grassroots Analytics has signed a 24,692-square-foot office lease spanning three floors at Arch Square in Downtown Washington, D.C., located at 803 Seventh Street NW. The company is more than doubling its footprint in the city, and the lease brings the mixed-use property—owned by Swiss real estate investment foundation AFIAA—to 100 percent office occupancy. D.C.'s office leasing market showed 21 percent growth in third-quarter volume, signaling market improvement.
stories.impact: Marginal relevance to multifamily. However, signs of D.C. office leasing recovery and mixed-use demand stabilization suggest institutional confidence in Downtown D.C. submarkets may support mixed-use development (office + residential) pipelines. Sustained office demand could reduce conversion pressure on office-to-residential projects, preserving capital discipline in multifamily development decisions in the nation's capital.

stories.title: Juda Chetrit Seals $55M Recap for 1384 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Juda Chetrit’s Chetrit Organization has secured a $55 million loan to recapitalize 1384 Broadway, Commercial Observer has learned. Maxim Capital Group provided the loan for the 80 percent occupied office building at Broadway and West 38th Street in Midtown Manhattan, sources familiar with the deal told CO. The transaction includes capital for lobby renovations, upgraded amenities and lease-up of the 204,034-square-foot tower. Iron Hound Management negotiated the recap. Iron Hound, Maxim and Chetrit declined to comment. Chetrit sealed the fresh capital for 1384 Broadway nearly a year after a previous $88 million commercial mortgage-backed securities loan, securitized in the CD 2017-CD3 conduit deal, hit special servicing in December 2025. The loan remained current as the borrower sought to finalize a discounted payoff before the end of 2026, according to David Putro, head of commercial real estate analytics at Morningstar Credit Analytics. That payoff is now completed. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Juda Chetrit secures $55M loan from Maxim Capital to recapitalize 1384 Broadway, Midtown Manhattan.
80% occupied office tower (204,034 SF) at Broadway/West 38th; capital for lobby, amenities, lease-up.
Refinance closes previous CMBS special servicing; prior $88M securitization hit special servicing Dec 2025.
stories.summary: Juda Chetrit's Chetrit Organization secured a $55 million loan from Maxim Capital Group to recapitalize 1384 Broadway, an 80 percent occupied office tower (204,034 square feet) at Broadway and West 38th Street in Midtown Manhattan. The financing provides capital for lobby renovations, upgraded amenities, and lease-up of remaining space. The transaction closes out a prior $88 million CMBS loan that had hit special servicing in December 2025.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. Successful rescue financing of distressed Midtown office asset indicates selective debt availability for high-quality assets in trophy locations, but caps broader office market stress. Flight of capital to selective trophy office assets reduces dry powder for multifamily refinancing in secondary markets; expect tighter multifamily financing terms as lenders concentrate exposure in office workout situations.

stories.title: Colliers Grows NYC Office, Industrial Leasing Teams With Two New Hires
stories.excerpt: Colliers is growing its New York City office and industrial leasing teams with two new hires, Commercial Observer has learned. Following a nearly seven-and-a-half-year tenure with Cushman & Wakefield, John Albal has joined Colliers as a senior associate within its Manhattan office and will focus on tenant representation and office leasing in Manhattan, according to Colliers. Meanwhile, Joseph Hentze Jr., a nearly six-year veteran at C&W, is joining the Manhattan office at Colliers as a vice president focusing on industrial leasing across the five boroughs. “John and Joseph bring valuable experience, strong client relationships and a deep understanding of the New York market to our team,” John Gallagher, executive managing director at Colliers in New York, said in a statement. “As companies continue to reassess their needs and make more strategic decisions about their real estate, having experienced advisers who can navigate an evolving market is more important than ever.” C&W declined CO’s request for comment. While Albal was with C&W, he specialized in tenant representation and advised C-suite executives regarding leasing opportunities and real estate strategies. “Colliers brings together a strong tenant representation business, deep market research and a respected global brand,” Albal said in a statement. “I’m excited to bring those resources to our clients and contribute to the firm’s continued growth in New York.” Hentze was most recently a director with C&W, where he advised both tenants and landlords on industrial leasing deals across Manhattan and the outer boroughs. “New York City’s industrial market presents a unique set of opportunities for businesses seeking space across the boroughs,” Hentze said in a statement. “I look forward to leveraging Colliers’ platform to help industrial owners and occupiers navigate their decisions and find properties that support their operational needs and long-term growth.&#82
bullets: Colliers hires John Albal (ex-Cushman & Wakefield) as senior associate, Manhattan office leasing.
Colliers adds Joseph Hentze Jr. (ex-C&W, 6 years) as VP, industrial leasing across 5 boroughs.
Broker recruitment reflects elevated tenant advisory demand as firms reassess real estate strategy.
stories.summary: Colliers has expanded its New York City office and industrial leasing teams with two senior hires from Cushman & Wakefield. John Albal, a 7.5-year veteran of C&W specializing in tenant representation and C-suite advisory, joined Colliers as a senior associate focused on Manhattan office leasing. Joseph Hentze Jr., a 6-year C&W veteran, joined as a vice president focusing on industrial leasing across the five boroughs. Leadership attributed the hires to rising demand for experienced advisers as companies reassess real estate needs.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. However, elevated broker recruitment and emphasis on tenant advisory services signal corporate real estate decision-making acceleration in NYC—potentially triggering office rightsizing and workforce mobility. Displaced office workers may increase demand for flexible, transit-proximate multifamily housing in Manhattan and outer-borough submarkets with strong transit access, indirectly supporting demand fundamentals for new residential development.
